pieces.content:
Turtles are under water, and
some turtle is punctured right through by a line.
The line had gone through through the turtle colony.
This turtle moved on the line, as if hosting an intestine,
    as if moving left when the line moved left.
It could see an independent turtle on another intestine
    and spiralled regularly around it.

We are we, and
we think of water as moving on a 3D conveyor belt, and
we think of turtles underwater as entangled with us priorly, and
we think of Hermes as an entangled line and a turtle, and
we think of fibrous light as an opening.

I am yours, and
the body part of the turtle urges itself around the line.
This roulette of turtles spirals around us syntotically now.
Intraction swings under water into info.
We tell turtles what to do.
We spill our guts.

parent.content: I placed the call to you, from Argyll to I think Caen —— it rang, went through, but was otherwise soundless —— I could have known that you were there —– but the cable was dropped to connect in the ocean too long ago —— falling sharks in the channel had bitten into it in parts —— salinity wore through it in parts —— engineers who in the first place on each part on either side disagreed on every standard of voltage and who couldn't talk in a Seaspeak anyway —— in channels the draghead and davits of dredging machines had torn or tangled the manila yarn which insulated a connection —— turned dark blue from holding its breath —— taking into account the way that with every word in a rail crash across a language barrier the situation worsens —— and again with the channel sharks falling —— there was enough of an edge left for the format but not the consignment —— no gentle wires to the word en-Masse —— so no capacitive sense —— no your voice
parent.title: Underwater cabling

° Well I say you're full of shit! / tracking no reply! / taking care! °

We prototype a rock-spiked snowball, first scooped and proposed in 1950 (Δ67y). The snowball is bigger than the rock and goes on the outside. It is hand-scale. The rock is a dependent. Snow seems to come from nowhere. (You can dance as if you're collecting it.) We believe the rock-spiked snowball is a discretionary item and is backwards-compatible with other versions of snow. It fits in & out. You won't realise what has happened to you if you are hit with a rock-spiked snowball, but your development environment will disintegrate; along with your experience, the stairwell of the thrower, the Internet coats, capped tiles, etc, will be set outside, in a springy graph solution—until the ludi of community resolves and your heart is broken.

parent.content: "Not only that, but this instantaneous ruin presents whole new vistas to the imagination. Let me show you what I mean. Suppose you walk to another section while your lover waits for God. In this state, you no longer need to know what you think is important; you don’t need to know how the buildings here came together. And your shoes are too tight."
